visual_goal: Show the volume gradient: each step up summarizes by orders of magnitude, and a dotted drill-back path with keys must lead back down each step.
prompt: A left-to-right staircase of five blocks that shrink sharply from a huge block at the far left to a tiny block at the far right, each block standing a step higher than the previous one. Each block has a label and a volume underneath: the first and largest block, made of a dense mass of tiny dots, 'Operational events' with '1.1 billion a year'; next 'Subledger lines' with '3 million a day'; next 'GL lines' with '38,000 a day'; next 'Reconciled accounts' with '6,800 a month'; and at the far right the smallest block, a single neat document, 'Statements' with 'a few hundred lines'. Four solid blue arrows climb the staircase, one between each pair of neighbouring blocks, pointing right and up. Below them, four dotted orange arrows run back down, one between each pair of neighbouring blocks, pointing left and down, each dotted arrow carrying a small key icon. Exactly eight arrows.
alt: A staircase of shrinking blocks from 1.1 billion operational events a year through 3 million subledger lines and 38,000 GL lines a day to 6,800 reconciled accounts a month and a few hundred statement lines, with solid arrows summarizing upward and dotted arrows carrying keys back down.

visual_goal: Show the finance reference model: a six-layer stack from business event to published number, satellites attached at several layers, a data platform reading from layers but being the book for none, an integration plane carrying the arrows and a control plane governing every box.
prompt: A layered architecture illustration. In the centre, a stack of six wide horizontal slabs, bottom to top: 'Operational systems', 'Subledger layer', 'Accounting core', 'Close and consolidation', 'Planning', 'Reporting'. Short upward arrows connect each slab to the one above it. To the right of the stack, a tall narrow box 'Satellite services' with two double-headed arrows, one to 'Subledger layer' and one to 'Accounting core'. To the left of the stack, a cylinder 'Data platform' with a magnifying glass, receiving one arrow from 'Subledger layer' and one from 'Accounting core', and sending one arrow up into 'Planning'. Behind the slabs runs a vertical translucent teal pipe labeled 'Integration plane', which the arrows visibly pass through. A thin dashed orange frame surrounds the whole picture, with a small shield and the label 'Control plane' on its top edge.
alt: Six stacked layers from operational systems through subledger, accounting core, close and consolidation and planning up to reporting; satellite services attach to the subledger and accounting core, a data platform reads from them and feeds planning, an integration pipe carries the arrows and a control-plane frame surrounds everything.

visual_goal: Show Northmere's baseline on the reference model: Stayloft uses every layer, Wayfare posts summaries straight into its ledger, Tablekin goes through billing, and the three ledgers meet only at consolidation.
prompt: A bottom-to-top illustration with three vertical columns side by side, standing on three base boxes labeled 'Stayloft', 'Wayfare' and 'Tablekin'. Faint horizontal bands behind the columns mark the layers. In the 'Stayloft' column, one arrow goes up from the base into a box 'Subledger', and one arrow up from 'Subledger' into an open ledger book. In the 'Wayfare' column, the subledger band holds an empty dashed outline, and one long arrow goes up from the base past the empty outline straight into an open ledger book, labeled 'summaries'. In the 'Tablekin' column, one arrow goes up from the base into a box 'Billing', and one arrow up from 'Billing' into an open ledger book. So there are three separate open ledger books side by side, unconnected to one another. At the top, one wide box spanning all three columns labeled 'Consolidation', receiving one arrow from each of the three ledger books. Exactly eight arrows.
alt: Three brand columns: Stayloft flows through a subledger into its ledger, Wayfare posts summaries straight into its ledger past an empty subledger slot, Tablekin flows through billing into its ledger, and the three separate ledgers meet only at consolidation on top.
